title.narrative: Energy Community's Ukraine Energy Support Fund
Energy Communitys Fond för stöd till Ukrainas Energi infrastruktur

description.narrative:
In the changes to the letter of appropriation UD2023/02951, dated 23 February 2023, the government of Sweden tasked Sida to manage the pledge of MSEK 300 to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund under the administration of the Energy Community Secretariat (EnCS). The needs within the energy sector in Ukraine are immense. The intention of the Swedish financial support is that it will make a direct difference as it will be channeled towards investments and reparation of the country’s energy infrastructure. For more information, see: https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2023/02/regeringen-allokerar-ytterligare-ett-omfattande-stod-om-520-miljoner-till-ukraina/ https://www.esv.se/statsliggaren/regleringsbrev/?rbid=23675
The support will be earmarked for use for the procurement of Necessary Support which is necessary, directly or indirectly, for: • De-centralised renewable energy solutions, including solar panels and associated equipment and services, batteries, microgrids, energy-efficiency measures for including for social services and households; • Electricity transmission and distribution sector; • Repair of energy infrastructure vital from a gender perspective. The financial support shall not be used for: • the purchase of fossil Fuels or Equipment based on the combustion of fossil Fuels. • Capital inflow.

Sida fick i en ändring av regleringsbrevet UD2023/02951 daterat den 23 februari 2023 i uppdrag att kanalisera 300 MSEK till Ukraine Energy Support Fund som administreras av Energy Community Secretariat (EnCS). Behoven inom energisektorn i Ukraina är enorma. Avsikten med det svenska ekonomiska stödet är att det ska göra en direkt skillnad då det ska kanaliseras mot investeringar och reparation av landets energiinfrastruktur. Se mer: https://www.regeringen.se/pressmeddelanden/2023/02/regeringen-allokerar-ytterligare-ett-omfattande-stod-om-520-miljoner-till-ukraina/ och https://www.esv.se/statsliggaren/regleringsbrev/?rbid=23675
Stödet är öronmärkt för att användas för upphandling av nödvändigt stöd som är avgörande, direkt eller indirekt, för: -­ Decentraliserade lösningar för förnybar energi, inklusive solpaneler och tillhörande utrustning och tjänster, batterier, mikronät, åtgärder för energieffektivitet för sociala tjänster och hushåll; - Sektorn för överföring och distribution av el; -­ Reparation av energiinfrastruktur avgörande ur ett jämställdhetsperspektiv. Det ekonomiska stödet får inte användas till: -­ inköp av fossila bränslen eller utrustning baserad på förbränning av fossila bränslen. - Kapitalinflöde.

The overall objective of the Ukraine Energy Support Fund (UESF) is to ensure that the energy system in Ukraine is functioning in a stable manner, providing energy consumers with uninterrupted supply of electricity, which in turn enables a stable supply of heating, water, and sanitation services in the country.
The theory of change behind the UESF is that by providing assistance to energy-related companies in Ukraine, they will be able to procure services and replenish their stock of goods, such as equipment, repair materials, infrastructure components, and fuel, necessary to ensure the stable functioning of the energy system. This assistance will not only help these companies restore their operations but also enable them to upgrade their systems, which will help to increase their resilience to future challenges.
The UESF's specific objective is to restore the resilience of the Ukrainian energy system through support to energy-related companies.
The UESF aims to achieve this objective by providing assistance to companies to procure necessary goods and services to restore and upgrade their systems. This assistance will, in turn, ensure the stable functioning of the energy system and provide energy consumers with uninterrupted supply, contributing to the overall stability of the country.
The Swedish funds are to contribute to the UESF specific objective as well as to a component on solar microgrids in social infrastructure aiming to achieve an enhanced resilience to climate change, conflict, and increased energy independence of the social infrastructure in Ukraine. To achieve this latter outcome, the project will deliver renewable energy-based microgrid packages to supply electricity to social public buildings in Ukraine.

description.narrative:
Ukraine Energy Support Fund (UESF) is a multi donor fund that finances repairs of energy infrastructure that has been destroyed by Russian attacks. As of 31 December 2024, the UESF had 29 donors with contributions of a total of 945,9 MEUR. Sweden was the third largest donor with 1.6 billion SEK, divided in three agreements (contribution numbers 16641 (520 MSEK), 16934 (500 MSEK) and 17210 (581 MSEK)), of which the first is the general support to UESF and last two are stand-alone specific projects that are included within the UESF but are reported on separately to Sida. The UESF is managed by the Energy Community Secretariate (EnCS).
Output 1 infrastructure equipment
From the original Sida UESF agreement, 220 MSEK was earmarked towards this output. In December 2024, Sida made an additional contribution to the UESF Output 1 of another 220 MSEK, i.e. a total of 440 MSEK.
These activities are constituting a large part of the portfolio under the first area - Reconstruction - of the Strategy for Sweden's Reconstruction and Reform Cooperation with Ukraine 2023-2027, and specifically Strategy Goal 1.
Energy provision has been repared and restored in around 20 regions of Ukraine since 2022. The Sida support was directed towards 16 regions during 2024. 635 purchase contracts have been entered into by the UESF since its establishment. Critical equipment delivered includes gas turbines, transformers, high voltage switchgear, mobile cogenerator units and solar energy equipment for hospitals. The majority of the deliveries have been concentrated in regions hardest hit by the war, including Kharkiv and Mykolaiv.
Output 2: Ray of Hope
In the agreement between Sida and the Energy Community, 80 MSEK were earmarked for decentralised renewable energy solutions. Under 2024, the program "Ray of Hope" was developed with a total budget of 33 MEUR for installation of solar panels at hospitals. Altogether, eight donors are contributing to the project which at the moment is fully funded. 17 healthcare facilities are now completed and operational, 27 additional hospitals are at the stage of solar systems installation and 100 further sites are under contracting or design. Swedish funding is used alongside funding from other donors and will support at least 26 facilities.
